baseline.entry_point: DPR Reader relevance head -> Top-5 ordering
baseline.equivalence_test: Initial residual_scale=0 must reproduce the original Reader scores and stable Top-k exactly.

core_invariants: Scope remains fixed Top-50 -> Top-5; retrieval, production QORE path, Generator, evaluator, and answer path remain frozen.
The online head sees only Reader outputs and passage-token masks; Silver/gold labels, generated answers, and evaluator outputs are forbidden.
Raw Reader relevance remains the score anchor; the Q-ARCG residual is applicability-gated and bounded.
The quantum arm and a same-parameter-budget classical control use the same features, split, loss, optimizer, and seeds.
The synthetic preflight is not a utility result and does not authorize a full-data run.

interfaces.input_schema: Reader relevance/start/end logits plus passage-token mask for one fixed candidate cohort
interfaces.output_schema: per-candidate score, applicability gate, bounded residual, and deterministic Top-5 order
invariants: All candidate IDs/order are preserved until ranking.
Residual is zero at null initialization and bounded by configured score spread.
No post-selection label or generation field is accepted.

plugins.insertion_point: DPR Reader relevance head before Top-5 ordering
plugins.hypothesis: The historical Reader relevance ordering is the anchor that Q-ARCG must preserve or improve.
plugins.input_schema: Reader relevance logit and candidate identity/rank
plugins.output_schema: raw Reader score and stable Top-5 IDs
plugins.resource_estimate: No additional model pass; CPU sort after Reader inference

plugins.insertion_point: Inside the Reader scoring path after relevance/span heads and before Top-5 ordering
plugins.hypothesis: A learned applicability gate can open a bounded quantum residual only when span evidence is consistent enough to rescue an underestimated passage, avoiding the span-only false positives observed in the failed fixed fusion screen.
plugins.input_schema: Reader relevance/start/end logits, passage-token mask, candidate identity/rank
plugins.output_schema: final score, gate, bounded residual, quantum observables, stable Top-5 IDs
plugins.resource_estimate: One shallow four-qubit differentiable statevector head per Reader batch; no extra corpus pass

plugins.insertion_point: Same Reader head boundary as Q-ARCG
plugins.hypothesis: Any task utility gain must exceed a same-budget classical gated residual control before a quantum-specific claim is considered.
plugins.input_schema: Identical Reader features and candidate identity/rank
plugins.output_schema: classical control score, gate, bounded residual, stable Top-5 IDs
plugins.resource_estimate: CPU/Torch feature head with exactly the Q-ARCG trainable parameter count

composition.merge_rule: Each arm scores the same unchanged Reader candidate cohort; only the final Top-5 order is compared, and no arm feeds its output to another.
interaction_ablations: null Q-ARCG versus frozen Reader Top-k

validation.baseline_equivalence: Synthetic and Torch null paths reproduce the original Reader scores exactly.

reproducibility.dataset_identity: synthetic contract fixture only; no real data or model inference
reproducibility.environment: Python 3.10+; NumPy for contract checks; Torch only for optional differentiability check

recovery_contract.discriminating_intermediate_measurement: Gate-open rate and positive-pair rank rescue in the middle-relevance/low-disagreement stratum, compared with the frozen Reader and same-budget classical control.

limitations: This implementation and its preflight are L0 engineering evidence only; no real-data utility or quantum advantage is established.
A future real-data run must train/infer the head inside the DPR Reader path with a frozen split, matched classical control, and independent executor.
The fixed four-qubit statevector can be classically simulated; utility and parameter-budget evidence must precede any quantum-specific claim.
